s1_bill: One Hertz renter got this bill minutes after returning a car. Four hundred and forty dollars, for a one-inch scuff on a wheel. A House subcommittee chair says Hertz sends these bills without human review. The company has an AI scanner. The renter has a phone.
s2_idea: Twice gives the renter the same evidence. Take the same photo twice: when you move in, and when you move out. Twice lines the two photos up, finds what really changed, and signs the proof.
s3_capture: At move-in, the shutter waits until each photo is sharp and detailed enough to match months later. At move-out, a ghost of the first photo guides you back to the same angle, and the camera fires when OpenCV locks on.
s4_car: Here is a sample check. On the car, a reflection looks like damage. One photo cannot tell them apart, so the agent asks for one more, from a step to the side. A reflection moves with the camera. A scratch stays on the paint. So the reflection is ruled out, and the scratch is reported.
s5_room: In the living room, a plain image difference would also flag the new shadow. Twice compares structure and colour, ignores exposure and small shifts, and tests whether a smooth change of light explains the difference. The shadow is ruled out. The stain and the scuff stay.
s6_report: The report shows every change, every ruled-out shadow, and the measurements behind each one. Every photo is hashed on arrival, and the move-in set is signed before any move-out photo exists.
s7_verify: Anyone can download the evidence bundle and check it with the script inside, without trusting our server. Change one photo, and the check fails.
s8_cloud: Twice runs in one container on AWS Lambda. Photos go to S3 with Object Lock, and a KMS key signs every report. Claude on Bedrock names each change, but it can never delete one. Objects are checked with NanoDet on the new OpenCV 5 DNN engine, more than three times faster than the classic engine.
s9_numbers: On our synthetic benchmark, Twice finds eighty-eight percent of the damage, and every flag is real. On real photos of unchanged scenes, it raised no false alarm in twenty-two judged pairs. Every failure case is in the report.
s10_close: Your next move-out starts with today's photos. Take them twice.
